clusters.name: Walter's move to Sorrel Valley, 1952–1953
clusters.reason: Around Walter moving the family across the country in March 1952 and buying the orchard, within the year: June's homesickness and daily letters to her sister, Walter out in the trees from dark to dark with distance growing between them, Glen's fights at school, Walter's cutoff from his brother Harlan over their father's land money, June keeping to her bed for weeks that winter, rows between Walter and June over money for new trees, and June joining the church choir by September as her anxiety eased. Walter's move was a structural change that mattered to everyone; the shifts show a broad disturbance in the household, with each person's trouble emerging in the months after.

clusters.name: The orchard's failure, 1968–1969
clusters.reason: Around the orchard failing in May 1968 when the late frost took the whole crop and the bank called in the loan, within the year: Walter drinking heavily most nights by June, conflict between Walter and Glen over blame for the loan, Glen's overfunctioning by taking over the family's money and talks with the bank, Carl's asthma attacks worsening that winter, Nora beginning to wet the bed in April 1969, Ida's heart trouble found in May 1969, and Walter stopping drinking by October 1969 and taking work pruning other men's trees. The orchard's loss was the pivot; the shifts pile up as different people absorbed the strain.

clusters.name: Glen's job loss at the cannery, 1975–1976
clusters.reason: Around Glen losing his job when the Ridgeport cannery closed in February 1975, within the year: Glen out of work most of that year sitting in the truck in the yard for hours, loud fights between Glen and Marian at night over money, Marian taking a second job cleaning offices at night while overfunctioning, Nora stopping eating properly and losing weight that summer, Nora keeping to her room and distancing from Marian, Walter drinking again after six years off it by December 1975, and Nora eating again and making the track team by June 1976 when Glen started driving a delivery truck. You said this year stood out as the hardest: your father's joblessness and your parents' nightly fights were the turn, and your own eating stopped until he found work.

clusters.name: Wilma moving into Nora and Sam's house, 1990–1991
clusters.reason: Around Wilma selling her farm and moving into your house in January 1990, within the year: you and Wilma clashing over the children's bedtimes and meals, you working late and distancing from Sam to keep out of the kitchen rows, Sam taking his mother's side, Owen having tantrums at preschool and being sent home twice, Wilma taking over Lily's care, your eczema flaring on both hands, you and Sam having rows most nights by November, and your eczema clearing over the summer once Wilma took a flat in town in June 1991. Wilma's move into your home was the change; the shifts show how the household's balance tilted toward her and away from you until she left.
